title: Smoothed Score Queries and the Complexity of Sampling
topic: Probabilistic Methods->Monte Carlo and Sampling Methods
claim: A sampler's finite-bit communication can be framed as simulating a channel from a transcript plus shared randomness, so bit lower bounds apply.
layout: 2 stacked rows, left-to-right boxes, dashed arrows from shared randomness below
description: Two rows of rounded boxes joined by arrows, in black and white. The top row, titled "Original channel", shows input x, then a box for the true channel P_{Y|X}, then output Y. The bottom row, titled "Channel synthesis", shows a box "Alice knows x", then a transcript box with T = T(x,Z) ∈ 𝒯 and |𝒯| ≤ 2^Q, then a box "Bob outputs Ŷ(T,Z)". A box at the bottom labeled "common randomness Z ⊥ x" sends dashed arrows up to Alice and to Bob. abstract: We study the query complexity of sampling from high-dimensional Gaussian distributions using gradient information. In the standard oracle model, exact gradients expose only matrix-vector products with the precision matrix, leading to polynomial approximation barriers and a characteristic $\sqrtÎº$ dependence on the known spectral range. We show that this barrier disappears when the sampler is allowed to query smoothed scores, namely gradients of the logarithms of the Gaussian-convolved densities. For a centered Gaussian target with precision matrix $Î$, a smoothed-score query at noise level $Ï$ gives access to the resolvent $(Î+Ï^{-1}I)^{-1}$. Combining geometrically spaced noise levels with sinc-quadrature rational approximation, we obtain a sampler with $q=O((\logÎº+\log(e\sqrt d/Î´_{\rm TV}))\log(e\sqrt d/Î´_{\rm TV}))$ smoothed-score queries for total variation error $Î´_{\rm TV}$, improving the condition-number dependence from $\sqrtÎº$ to logarithmic. We also study finite-bit gradient oracles. Using coordinatewise quantization of the transformed smoothed-score answers and a final dithering step, we obtain a sampling scheme whose total communicated gradient information is polylogarithmic in $Îº$; in particular, for fixed dimension and accuracy, the bit complexity is $O(\log^2Îº)$. To complement these upper bounds, we introduce a channel-synthesis, or reverse-Shannon, converse technique for sampling lower bounds. This converts total-variation simulation guarantees into communication requirements and yields an $Î©(d\logÎº)$ bit lower bound for $d\ge2$ and fixed total variation error below one, as $Îº\to\infty$. Together, these results identify smoothed scores as a provably more informative oracle for sampling and give nearly matching upper and lower bounds for its finite-bit complexity.
